1	# Task 11: Polished car-paint object with clearcoat on a turntable
2	
3	Framework: Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules; three.js 0.185.1 is also installed for procedural asset factories, see BRIDGE.md).
4	
5	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, drawing into the existing canvas with id #app. Show a glossy, candy-red, car-paint finished object on a slowly rotating turntable in a dark showroom. Since no model files are provided, construct the object procedurally from smooth shapes, for example a rounded, streamlined capsule or bean body with a separate smooth cabin bump and four dark rubber wheel discs, or any other smooth body with clearly curved, large reflective panels. The paint must look like automotive paint: a deep coloured base layer with fine metallic flake sparkle, topped by a glossy clear coat that mirrors a studio environment (long soft-box strip reflections that bend over the curved panels). Add chrome trim, such as a thin ring or strip, and a dark glass or black cabin panel for contrast. The turntable is a circular platform with a subtle ring light or reflective floor on which the object is mirrored faintly. Use a dark background with two or three long strip lights above and to the sides, plus a faint cool rim light, so the reflections read as soft-box highlights. 1	# Aura3D

3	> Aura3D 5.5.0: a TypeScript SDK for browser 3D apps and games. You write a typed, declarative scene with `@aura3d/engine`; the `@aura3d/cli` toolchain handles typed GLB/glTF assets, checks and deploy gates. Built to be driven by AI coding agents. Site: https://aura3d.auraone.ai
4	
5	## First screen: Aura3D patterns (copy the shape, change the subject)
6	
7	`@aura3d/engine` is installed; never open `node_modules` or `dist`. Blocks are typechecked, GPU-rendered patterns, not finished scenes: change subject and numbers; typecheck once. `createAuraApp(selector, { scene })` owns renderer, resize and loop. Vectors `[x, y, z]`, colours CSS strings, primitives are unit shapes scaled by `size`. Per frame `app.onFrame((f) => ...)` gives `f.dt`, `f.time` in seconds. To change a node later give it `.runtime({ id, mutable: true })`, then `app.nodes.require(id).setPosition(x, y, z)`.
